symptom: `mxcli git commit` silently leaves a user file out of the commit when any folder on its path is named like a build folder: `resources/deployment/endpoints.xml` (or `javascriptsource/theme-cache/x.js`) stays untracked after the commit, with only `Left out 1 file(s) Studio Pro never commits (project-settings.user.json, *.mpr.lock, caches)` to show for it
cause: isJunkPath matched `.mendix-cache`, `deployment`, `theme-cache` and `.mxcli` on every path segment, so any folder of that name at any depth was dropped. Those are the project's own folders, the ones Studio Pro, mxbuild and mxcli create directly beside the .mpr; the file-name rules (lock, backup, user settings) are the ones that rightly match at any level
file: `cmd/mxcli/cmd_git_commit.go` (`isJunkPath(rel, projDir)`, projDir from `path.Dir(gitNoteRepo.MPRPath)`, which already resolves the project folder inside the repository, symlinks included); tests `TestGitCommit_NestedFolderNamedLikeJunkIsCommitted`, `TestGitCommit_JunkAnchoredAtProjectInSubfolder` in `cmd/mxcli/gitdoctor_test.go`
insight: **Anchor a path rule where the thing it names is created**: the build and cache folders only ever appear beside the .mpr, and a rule that matches the name at every depth also catches user folders that share it. **The report that something was left out did not name it**, which is what made the drop silent; a nested-folder fixture next to the root one (the existing test only had root `deployment/`) is the control that tells the two apart. Test the project-in-a-subfolder layout too: the anchor is the project's folder, not the repository root, and the same names outside the project are not its own
